# Rule index: nestjs

Every rule ID of the nestjs docs with its headline, grouped by doc. The headline is the rule's first sentence; the full rule (details, values, examples, *Why*) is in the doc. **Before you implement against a rule, read its full text**: search the doc for the ID and read that bullet, or read the doc when the task is centred on its topic. ## [NestJS: Libraries](../04-solution-strategy/nestjs-libraries.md)

- NEST-LIB-01: All `@nestjs/*` packages are on the same major (12), and versions are pinned exactly (TS-TOOL-13).
- NEST-LIB-02: TypeScript is pinned to 6.0.x.
- NEST-LIB-03: The HTTP platform is Fastify (`@nestjs/platform-fastify`).
- NEST-LIB-04: zod 4 is the only schema library.
- NEST-LIB-05: `reflect-metadata` is imported once, first thing in `main.ts` (and in the Vitest setup).
- NEST-LIB-06: Mapping is hand-written (ARCH-MAP-08).
- NEST-LIB-07: Outgoing HTTP calls use `fetch` and `Agent` imported from the `undici` package with explicit timeouts and an `AbortSignal` deadline per call (resilience/nestjs.md);
- NEST-LIB-08: Resilience policies use cockatiel, only in outgoing adapters.
- NEST-LIB-09: Database access uses Kysely with `pg`.
- NEST-LIB-10: Kafka uses `@platformatic/kafka` (pure JavaScript, no native build) in own messaging adapters.
- NEST-LIB-11: The service ships as a minimal, non-root OCI image with an SBOM (REL-IMG-01/02):

## [NestJS: Hexagonal Architecture](../05-building-block-view/nestjs.md)

- NEST-ARCH-01: Each bounded context has one Nest module, `<context>.module.ts`, as its composition root.
- NEST-ARCH-02: Core classes carry no decorators.
- NEST-ARCH-03: Tokens are `Symbol`s in `<context>.tokens.ts`, one per `ports/in` and `ports/out` contract (`export const PLACE_ORDER_USE_CASE = Symbol('PlaceOrderUseCase')`).
- NEST-ARCH-04: Constructor injection only, singleton scope only.
- NEST-ARCH-05: No `forwardRef`.
- NEST-ARCH-06: Global concerns are registered once in `app.module.ts` via `APP_FILTER`, `APP_PIPE`, `APP_GUARD` (problem-details filter, `StandardSchemaValidationPipe`, auth guard).
- NEST-ARCH-07: `create-app.ts` builds the application; `main.ts` only starts it.
- NEST-ARCH-08: The use case owns the transaction through an outgoing port (ARCH-UC-11).
- NEST-ARCH-09: Use cases never call each other, also not through `@nestjs/event-emitter` or RxJS subjects (ARCH-UC-14).
- NEST-ARCH-10: Controllers are incoming adapters in `adapter/in/rest/v<N>`, one controller per use case or small group of use cases on the same resource.
- NEST-ARCH-11: Third-party SDK types never leave their adapter folder (ARCH-DEP-05):
- NEST-ARCH-12: Every incoming adapter maps the error categories by their base classes (ARCH-UC-13, NODE-ARCH-07):
- NEST-ARCH-13: Demo and seed data of a running installation are loaded by an incoming adapter that calls the use cases.

## [NestJS: Delivery](../07-deployment-view/nestjs-delivery.md)

- NEST-REL-01: By default the new version migrates at start-up, before it listens; from the second instance or the first production environment the pre-deploy variant (NEST-REL-03) is required.
- NEST-REL-02: Parallel instances and the start-up budget.
- NEST-REL-03: The pre-deploy variant runs the same image with `node dist/migrate.js` (REL-DB-01).
- NEST-REL-04: A migration needs no other tool in the pipeline:
- NEST-REL-05: The process is `node`, started in exec form, never through `npm start` or a shell (npm does not forward signals):
- NEST-REL-06: The image does not carry the release version; the deployment injects it (REL-CD-01).
- NEST-REL-07: NestJS services build their image with the Dockerfile of NEST-REL-08, not with Buildpacks.
- NEST-REL-08: The Dockerfile is multi-stage, from lockfile, on distroless, pinned by digest (template: `.agents/skills/baseline-nestjs/templates/Dockerfile`).
- NEST-REL-09: The container runs with a read-only root filesystem and a size-limited `/tmp` (REL-RUN-01/02).
- NEST-REL-10: When the NestJS backend is the BFF, the image build adds the bundle as `frontend/` next to `dist/`.
- NEST-REL-12: The bundle folder is checked at start and the image is smoke-tested (REL-FE-06).
- NEST-REL-11: The release job publishes a CycloneDX SBOM of the image (REL-IMG-01), generated from the image by the pipeline's image scanner, and the dependency SBOM of TS-TOOL-16 (`@cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm --omit dev`).

## [NestJS: Local Development](../07-deployment-view/nestjs-local-development.md)

- NEST-DEV-01: `backend/compose.yaml` defines every infrastructure dependency the service uses.
- NEST-DEV-02: Core services (database, broker) have no Compose profile and start by default.
- NEST-DEV-03: Images are pinned, ports bind to `127.0.0.1`, credentials are throwaway.
- NEST-DEV-04: Local PostgreSQL has the production role split.
- NEST-DEV-05: Kafka is a single-node KRaft broker on the fixed host port 9092.
- NEST-DEV-06: Local configuration is the committed `.env.local` (NEST-CFG-06):
- NEST-DEV-07: The Node version comes from `.nvmrc` (`nvm use`, `fnm use` or the IDE), the same major as CI and the image (NODE-TOOL-01).
- NEST-DEV-08: `npm run start:dev` is `nest start --watch --env-file .env.local`.
- NEST-DEV-09: Debugging uses `npm run start:debug` = `nest start --watch --debug --env-file .env.local`, which adds `--inspect` (inspector on `127.0.0.1:9229`);
- NEST-DEV-10: No bash or PowerShell start-up scripts.
- NEST-DEV-11: A frontend developer gets a working backend with `cd backend && docker compose up -d --wait && npm ci && npm run start:dev`, or the built image with Compose (NEST-DEV-12).
- NEST-DEV-12: The `e2e:smoke` job runs the application image of the same commit next to the local services with Docker Compose (REPO-CI-04):

## [NestJS: Producing the OpenAPI Contract (code-first)](../08-crosscutting-concepts/api/nestjs-openapi.md)

- NEST-API-01: The `operationId` is the handler method name (API-CON-05), set for all operations by `operationIdFactory` in the builder.
- NEST-API-02: Every request, response and enum schema has an id unique per API version:
- NEST-API-03: Required means required.
- NEST-API-04: zod constraints are part of the contract (`min`, `max`, `regex`, `z.uuid()`, `z.iso.*`) and appear as schema constraints, so clients validate the same way.
- NEST-API-05: Every error status an operation can return is documented as `application/problem+json` (API-CON-05, API-REST-05/07) with the shared decorator, listing the business codes.
- NEST-API-06: Schemas carry examples (API-CON-05, API-CON-11) with `.meta({ example })`, so generated mocks are realistic.
- NEST-API-07: Responses are declared with `standardSchema` (`@ApiOkResponse({ standardSchema: X })`, `@ApiCreatedResponse(…)`).
- NEST-API-08: `@nestjs/swagger` is imported only in `adapter/in/rest` and `src/platform/adapter/in/rest`, never in `domain`, `ports` or `application`;
- NEST-API-09: A test builds the spec and fails if the committed file is stale (API-CON-03).
- NEST-API-10: CI runs `oasdiff` against the target branch (API-CON-04), from the backend folder:
- NEST-API-11: The application does not serve its spec or Swagger UI.
- NEST-API-12: Every new read endpoint gets the N+1 check (API-CON-06, API-N1-01):
- NEST-API-13: Clients for providers with a spec are generated with Orval (API-CON-07, NEST-LIB rules in 04-solution-strategy/nestjs-libraries.md):
- NEST-API-14: The outgoing adapter owns the generated client and never lets its types out (API-CON-09, ARCH-ADP-12).

## [NestJS: REST and JSON Conventions](../08-crosscutting-concepts/api/nestjs-rest.md)

- NEST-REST-01: One controller per use case (or a small cohesive group) in `adapter/in/rest/vN/`, with its own request and response zod schemas (ARCH-ADP-03/04).
- NEST-REST-02: Mapping is hand-written in the controller folder.
- NEST-REST-03: URLs are plural nouns in kebab-case with the version prefix in the controller path (`@Controller('v1/orders')`).
- NEST-REST-04: Versioning is by version folder and path prefix (ARCH-ORG-03).
- NEST-REST-05: Fastify types only; no `@Res()` without passthrough.
- NEST-REST-06: Every body, query and path parameter has a zod schema on its decorator:
- NEST-REST-07: One global `StandardSchemaValidationPipe` with an `exceptionFactory` turns zod issues into the 400 problem of API-REST-05.
- NEST-REST-08: Unknown request properties are stripped, not rejected (API-REST-04).
- NEST-REST-09: Regular expressions in request schemas are anchored, simple and length-bounded (`max()` before `regex()`), because a catastrophic backtracking pattern blocks the event loop for every request (ReDoS, NEST-SEC-24 in security/nestjs-hardening.md).
- NEST-REST-10: Decimals and money use the shared `ApiDecimal` schema, never `z.number()` (API-REST-01).
- NEST-REST-11: Date and time (API-REST-02):
- NEST-REST-12: Enums are `z.enum([...])` with `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` values and an id (`.meta({ id: 'OrderStatusV1' })`, API-REST-03).
- NEST-REST-13: Optional response fields are left `undefined`, never `null` (API-REST-04).
- NEST-REST-14: Errors are RFC 9457 problems from one global exception filter (API-REST-05/06, ARCH-ADP-05):
- NEST-REST-15: Fastify's errors and those of its plugins become problems too.
- NEST-REST-16: A raw `ZodError` never reaches the filter.
- NEST-REST-17: Collection endpoints are paged with a hard maximum `size`, or bounded by a documented upper limit that the query enforces (API-REST-08, API-N1-07).
- NEST-REST-18: Updates to concurrently changed resources use optimistic concurrency (API-REST-11), with the version in the body or as a strong `ETag`.
- NEST-REST-19: A `201 Created` sets `Location` (API-REST-06):
- NEST-REST-20: A deprecated operation is marked `@ApiOperation({ deprecated: true, description: '<replacement>' })` and sends the `Deprecation` header (`@Header('Deprecation', '@<unix-seconds>')`), plus `Sunset` and `Link` once the removal date is fixed (API-REST-12).
- NEST-REST-21: Controller tests run the controller in Nest with the Fastify adapter and a mocked use case (TEST-ARCH-03, NEST-TEST rules in testing/nestjs.md):

## [NestJS: Configuration](../08-crosscutting-concepts/configuration/nestjs.md)

- NEST-CFG-01: Each configuration area is one zod object schema, parsed once at start-up into a frozen, typed object (CFG-08).
- NEST-CFG-02: `src/platform/config/load-config.ts` is the only code that reads `process.env` (NODE-ARCH-12, CFG-09).
- NEST-CFG-03: A configuration object reaches its adapter through a token, provided by the context module:
- NEST-CFG-04: `@nestjs/config` is not used.
- NEST-CFG-05: Keys are the environment variable names:
- NEST-CFG-06: Deployed environments differ only in injected values (CFG-02/04).
- NEST-CFG-07: Secrets come from files mounted by the platform (CFG-05):
- NEST-CFG-08: Every secret value has the type `Secret` (CFG-07), produced by the `secret()` schema helper.
- NEST-CFG-09: Configuration is never dumped:
- NEST-CFG-12: `secret(minLength)` states the strength of a secret, and keys with a format state it in the schema.
- NEST-CFG-13: Switches that only make sense locally are refused in a deployed environment.
- NEST-CFG-10: `configuration-keys.yaml` in `backend/` lists every key a deployment sets (CFG-12):
- NEST-CFG-11: A NestJS BFF serves `GET /config.json` (CFG-11) from a validated `FRONTEND_*` schema, mapped to an explicit response schema (never a dump of the environment or of a configuration object).

## [NestJS: Data Protection](../08-crosscutting-concepts/data-protection/nestjs.md)

- NEST-DP-01: A retention job is an incoming adapter in `adapter/in/scheduling`:
- NEST-DP-02: Deletion runs in bounded batches, one transaction per batch.
- NEST-DP-03: Child tables owned by the person reference their parent with `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the migration (`.references('customer_accounts.id').onDelete('cascade')`).
- NEST-DP-04: History, messaging and idempotency stores are part of erasure and retention:
- NEST-DP-05: Each context that stores personal data publishes an exporter and an eraser.
- NEST-DP-06: Events are keyed by the person's or aggregate's id and carry personal fields only where the consumer needs them.
- NEST-DP-07: Personal data never reaches logs, spans or metric labels (DP-TEL-01).
- NEST-DP-08: Retention, export and erasure adapters are tested against Testcontainers PostgreSQL with the real migrations (NEST-DB-22) as `*.it.test.ts`:
- NEST-DP-09: Code that handles personal data has a test asserting it does not reach the log (DP-TEST-02, NEST-LOG-10):
- NEST-DP-10: By default an insert-only audit table is partitioned by month and purged by dropping partitions.

## [NestJS: Internationalization](../08-crosscutting-concepts/i18n/nestjs.md)

- NEST-I18N-01: Server texts are ICU MessageFormat strings, formatted with `intl-messageformat` 12; `nestjs-i18n` is not used.
- NEST-I18N-02: One catalog per supported locale, nested JSON with ICU messages, in `src/platform/adapter/i18n/messages/<locale>.json`.
- NEST-I18N-03: The locale of a response comes from `Accept-Language`, negotiated in the REST adapter only.
- NEST-I18N-04: In a multilingual product, `ProblemDetailsFilter` keeps the stable `code` and localizes `title` and `detail`.
- NEST-I18N-05: Locale code and locale-dependent calls never appear in `domain`, `ports` or `application`.
- NEST-I18N-06: Outgoing adapters render emails and documents in the recipient's stored language and time zone, never the request locale.
- NEST-I18N-07: The API never formats values for display (I18N-03):
- NEST-I18N-08: Server-side sorting that users see uses an explicit ICU collation per locale in the query (`order by name collate "de-x-icu"`;

## [NestJS: Logging](../08-crosscutting-concepts/logging/nestjs.md)

- NEST-LOG-01: pino through `nestjs-pino` is the only logger (NEST-D11).
- NEST-LOG-02: Logs are JSON lines on stdout in every environment, one object per line with `level`, `time`, `msg`, `context`.
- NEST-LOG-03: Every line written inside a request, message or job carries `traceId` and `spanId` through a pino `mixin` that reads the active OpenTelemetry span.
- NEST-LOG-04: The level is configuration:
- NEST-LOG-05: Request lines contain method, path, status and duration, nothing else from the request.
- NEST-LOG-06: Values go into the object argument, the message is a constant text:
- NEST-LOG-07: Where logging happens:
- NEST-LOG-08: An error is logged once, where it is handled:
- NEST-LOG-09: Never log secrets, tokens, passwords, session contents, full request or response bodies, or personal data.
- NEST-LOG-10: Logs are asserted only where they matter:

## [NestJS: Messaging with Kafka](../08-crosscutting-concepts/messaging/nestjs.md)

- NEST-MSG-01: Kafka is used through `@platformatic/kafka` 2.15.0 (Apache-2.0, pinned exactly), with its `Producer`, `Consumer` and `Admin` classes, in our own adapters.
- NEST-MSG-02: The client installs with `ignore-scripts=true` and needs no build step (NODE-TOOL-08 in node-tooling.md).
- NEST-MSG-03: Consumers live in `adapter/in/messaging/`, producers in `adapter/out/messaging/`; shared Kafka plumbing lives in the platform rings.
- NEST-MSG-04: A consumer dispatches on the envelope `type`, maps and calls one incoming port.
- NEST-MSG-05: Client settings are explicit, in one factory in `src/platform/adapter/out/messaging/`.
- NEST-MSG-06: Payloads are UTF-8 JSON in `Buffer`s, typed and checked by zod.
- NEST-MSG-07: One consumer runner reads each stream sequentially, classifies errors by category and never lets an error leave the loop.
- NEST-MSG-08: Dead letters go to the consumer's own topic, keep the record and are counted.
- NEST-MSG-09: The outbox writer inserts into the use case's transaction.
- NEST-MSG-10: One relay instance sends the outbox in order per key and parks what can never be sent.
- NEST-MSG-15: A side effect after commit without a broker (an e-mail, a call to an external system) uses the same outbox shape inside its own adapter.
- NEST-MSG-11: Consumers deduplicate through an inbox port unless the use case is naturally idempotent (MSG-IDM-01/02;
- NEST-MSG-12: Consumers start after bootstrap and stop first on shutdown, within 20 s.
- NEST-MSG-13: The AsyncAPI document is generated by a script from the adapter's zod schemas and checked like the OpenAPI spec (MSG-CON-01).
- NEST-MSG-14: Kafka adapter tests are `*.it.test.ts` with `KafkaContainer` from `@testcontainers/kafka` 12 (testing/nestjs.md).

## [NestJS: Observability and Operability](../08-crosscutting-concepts/observability/nestjs.md)

- NEST-OBS-01: `/livez` and `/readyz` are served by the application's own HTTP server on the server port (OBS-19, realisation a), so a probe passes only if the listener that serves users works.
- NEST-OBS-02: Liveness is a plain handler without checks (OBS-02):
- NEST-OBS-03: Readiness is a Terminus check of the primary database only, and only where OBS-03 applies.
- NEST-OBS-04: Shutdown follows Nest's hook order, with a drain before the server closes (OBS-04).
- NEST-OBS-05: OpenTelemetry starts in `src/instrumentation.ts`, loaded with `--import` before any application module.
- NEST-OBS-06: Telemetry is configured per environment through `OTEL_*` variables (CFG-03, OBS-13), listed in `configuration-keys.yaml`:
- NEST-OBS-07: Technical metrics come from the instrumentations (OBS-06).
- NEST-OBS-08: Business metrics go through an outgoing port (OBS-07, OBS-09):
- NEST-OBS-09: Outbound calls and messages carry the trace.
- NEST-OBS-10: Error responses return the trace id.
- NEST-OBS-11: Operability is tested:

## [NestJS: Persistence with PostgreSQL](../08-crosscutting-concepts/persistence/nestjs.md)

- NEST-DB-01: PostgreSQL 18 is the engine, in the same major version everywhere (production, `compose.yaml`, Testcontainers).
- NEST-DB-02: Schema conventions:
- NEST-DB-03: Types cross the driver without loss.
- NEST-DB-04: One `Kysely<DB>` instance and one `pg.Pool` per process, created in `database.ts` from the database config schema and provided by the platform persistence module;
- NEST-DB-05: Table types are generated from the migrated schema, never written by hand.
- NEST-DB-06: Rows never cross a port; persistence always uses two-way mapping.
- NEST-DB-07: Queries are built with Kysely's builder or the `sql` template tag, values always as bind parameters (NEST-SEC-25).
- NEST-DB-08: The use case sets the boundary with `TransactionPort.runInTransaction(work)`; the Kysely adapter keeps the open transaction in `AsyncLocalStorage`.
- NEST-DB-09: A conflict re-runs the whole unit of work (RES-RTY-02):
- NEST-DB-10: Optimistic locking uses a `version integer not null default 0` column on aggregates that users change concurrently.
- NEST-DB-11: Driver errors are mapped in the adapter, never passed through the port (ARCH-ADP-01):
- NEST-DB-23: An invariant across rows holds under concurrency through one of these PostgreSQL mechanisms (ARCH-UC-16), named in the use case's comment:
- NEST-DB-12: No query per item.
- NEST-DB-13: Every collection query is bounded in the query itself (API-REST-08, API-N1-07):
- NEST-DB-14: Migrations are TypeScript files run by `Migrator` from `kysely/migration` (not from `kysely`, 0.29 moved it), listed statically in `migrations/index.ts` (no `FileMigrationProvider`, so `dist/` needs no directory scan), with `allowUnorderedMigrations: false`.
- NEST-DB-15: What the Kysely migrator does on PostgreSQL (Kysely 0.29.9, verified):
- NEST-DB-16: The migration connection is its own one-connection pool with the DDL user and two session timeouts:
- NEST-DB-17: Two database users (REL-DB-01):
- NEST-DB-18: `assertSchemaCurrent()` compares the static list with `migrator.getMigrations()` (each entry has `executedAt`) using the DML user, and throws when a migration is pending.
- NEST-DB-19: Migrations are immutable once on `main`, checked in CI.
- NEST-DB-20: Migrations are compatible with the previous release (expand/contract, REL-DB-02):
- NEST-DB-21: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` cannot run in the default transactional run (it fails with SQLSTATE `25001`).
- NEST-DB-22: Every persistence test runs the real migrations against Testcontainers PostgreSQL (`@testcontainers/postgresql`, image `postgres:18`).

## [NestJS: Resilience and Idempotency](../08-crosscutting-concepts/resilience/nestjs.md)

- NEST-RES-01: Every outbound call has explicit timeouts, set from configuration (RES-TMO-01/02):
- NEST-RES-02: Every HTTP adapter has a timeout test against a delaying stub (RES-TMO-03):
- NEST-RES-03: Remote calls run before or after the transaction, never inside it (RES-TX-01).
- NEST-RES-04: The pg pool is the database limit; its size is explicit and its wait is short.
- NEST-RES-05: Each remote dependency gets a bulkhead that rejects:
- NEST-RES-06: A circuit breaker, where RES-CAP-03 calls for one, uses cockatiel and is shared by all calls of the adapter:
- NEST-RES-07: Retries are a cockatiel policy in the outgoing adapter, with a filter, jittered backoff and a total timeout:
- NEST-RES-08: An adapter called from a message consumer does not retry;
- NEST-RES-09: The REST adapter reads `Idempotency-Key` and passes it in the command as a core value object.
- NEST-RES-10: The idempotency table is a Kysely migration (../persistence/nestjs.md):
- NEST-RES-11: Jobs are `@Cron` methods in `adapter/in/scheduling`, call an incoming port, and run under a cluster lock (RES-JOB-01/02).
- NEST-RES-12: Jobs are tested as adapters:
- NEST-RES-13: CPU-heavy work runs in worker threads, behind an outgoing port (NODE-ARCH-10).
- NEST-RES-14: Caches are `lru-cache` instances inside the outgoing adapter (RES-CCH-01/03), with both `max` and `ttl` set (the library rejects a cache with neither, but `ttl` alone does not bound memory).
- NEST-RES-15: Bulk use cases hand per-item remote calls to a job (RES-JOB-04):

## [NestJS: Hardening](../08-crosscutting-concepts/security/nestjs-hardening.md)

- NEST-SEC-20: `createApp()` registers `@fastify/helmet` 13 for the whole app; no route turns it off (`helmet: false` is forbidden).
- NEST-SEC-21: TLS everywhere outside the developer machine, with the versions of SEC-CRY-01.
- NEST-SEC-22: Request limits are set explicitly on `new FastifyAdapter({...})` from configuration, not left to defaults:
- NEST-SEC-23: Untrusted JSON is parsed strictly and never merged into existing objects.
- NEST-SEC-24: No regular expression comes from user input, and every regex that sees user input is linear.
- NEST-SEC-25: Queries receive user-influenced values only as bind parameters.
- NEST-SEC-26: No dynamic code.
- NEST-SEC-27: Request schemas carry only what the caller may set.
- NEST-SEC-28: A multi-tenant product takes the tenant only from the `Caller` (a token claim mapped by the guard), never from a path, query parameter or body.
- NEST-SEC-29: An object the caller may not see answers 404, as if it did not exist; 403 only when the caller may know the object but lacks the permission for this action (may read an order, may not cancel it).
- NEST-SEC-30: Responses never contain stack traces, SQL, class names or exception messages.
- NEST-SEC-31: Outbound HTTP to a destination that users or data influence is restricted:
- NEST-SEC-32: Rate limiting answers 429 and sits at the gateway or reverse proxy by default.
- NEST-SEC-33: Security events are logged as structured audit events:
- NEST-SEC-34: An unhandled rejection or uncaught exception ends the process.
- NEST-SEC-35: Nothing CPU-heavy or synchronous runs on the event loop in a request path:
- NEST-SEC-36: Deployed environments run only production code:
- NEST-SEC-37: Uploads are limited and stored, scanned and served so that a file cannot attack the server or other users:
- NEST-SEC-38: The application's database role has DML rights only;
- NEST-SEC-39: Kafka in non-local environments uses TLS, SASL, ACLs per service and no auto-created topics.
- NEST-SEC-40: The image meets REL-IMG-01 and REL-RUN-01/02:
- NEST-SEC-41: Consider Node's permission model for services with a narrow footprint: `node --permission --allow-fs-read=/app --allow-net dist/main.js` (plus `--allow-fs-write=/tmp` if needed).
- NEST-SEC-42: Cryptography follows SEC-CRY-01..05 with `node:crypto` and `jose` only:
- NEST-SEC-43: The npm supply-chain rules of TS-TOOL-11..16 (typescript-tooling.md) apply to the backend unchanged:
- NEST-SEC-44: The BFF implements NODE-BFF-01.
- NEST-SEC-45: The OIDC login of NODE-BFF-02 lives in a BFF controller in `adapter/in/rest`.
- NEST-SEC-46: The session store of NODE-BFF-03 is `@fastify/session` 11 (with `@fastify/cookie` 11) with a store object implementing `set`, `get`, `compareAndSet` (`ENOENT` on a missing session or a generation mismatch) and `destroy`.
- NEST-SEC-47: The cookie of NODE-BFF-04 is configured as `cookieName: '__Host-session'`, `cookie: { path: '/', httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'lax' }` without `domain`, and cleared with `secure: true`, `path: '/'`.
- NEST-SEC-48: CSRF (NODE-BFF-06) uses `@fastify/csrf-protection` 8 with `sessionPlugin: '@fastify/session'` and `getToken: (req) => req.headers['x-xsrf-token']` (the default also reads the body and other headers).
- NEST-SEC-49: Lifetimes and refresh (NODE-BFF-07) run in an `onRequest` hook that checks `lastSeenAt` and `createdAt` in the session;
- NEST-SEC-50: Logout (NODE-BFF-08) calls `request.session.destroy()` and clears the cookie as in NEST-SEC-47; the back-channel endpoint is a `@Public()` route with a body limit.
- NEST-SEC-51: The BFF serves the SPA (NODE-BFF-09, REL-FE-01..05 in container-runtime.md) with `@fastify/static` 10 (an exact-version dependency added together with this serving code; the service skeleton does not contain it) and helmet's CSP directive functions:
- NEST-SEC-52: The NestJS BFF meets NODE-BFF-10, and its end-to-end test also checks every header of NEST-SEC-20.

## [NestJS: Security](../08-crosscutting-concepts/security/nestjs.md)

- NEST-SEC-01: One global `AuthGuard` authenticates every request; endpoints are protected unless marked `@Public()`.
- NEST-SEC-02: The REST adapter authenticates, the use case authorizes.
- NEST-SEC-03: The backend API is an OAuth2 resource server as soon as a non-browser client calls it (a separate BFF, another service, a script), and it verifies JWTs with `jose` 6 and nothing else.
- NEST-SEC-04: `jwtVerify` pins every check explicitly:
- NEST-SEC-05: No `passport` and no `@nestjs/passport`.
- NEST-SEC-06: Stateless token APIs need no CSRF protection; a cookie-authenticated route always has it (BFF, NEST-SEC-48).
- NEST-SEC-07: CORS is configured once with `app.enableCors({ origin: [...], credentials })` (Nest's Fastify adapter registers `@fastify/cors` 11.4) in `createApp()`, with the origins from configuration.
- NEST-SEC-08: Every use case that takes a caller-supplied id checks owner or tenant, and a test proves that user A cannot read or change user B's resource.
- NEST-SEC-09: Secrets and tokens never reach a log, a response or the repository (SEC-INC-01, CFG-05, CFG-07).
- NEST-SEC-10: Probe and operational endpoints expose nothing and are not routed from outside.
- NEST-SEC-11: Fastify's `trustProxy` is set explicitly per deployment, never left to chance:
- NEST-SEC-12: Browser applications authenticate through a backend-for-frontend (BFF) that performs the OIDC login, keeps the tokens server-side and gives the browser only a session cookie with CSRF protection.
- NEST-SEC-13: Whether the BFF is its own component (`backend-bff/`, REPO-LAY-03) or a module of the NestJS backend is decided per project in an ADR.
- NEST-SEC-53: Users the product administers are provisioned in the IdP through an outgoing port, never by a second user store with passwords:
- NEST-SEC-14: Every endpoint has security tests for 401 (no or invalid token), 403 (insufficient role, where coarse roles apply) and the success case.
- NEST-SEC-15: Authorization rules are unit-tested on `Caller` in the use-case tests, without a Nest context (London style for the ports, TEST-TDD;

## [Node.js Backend-for-Frontend](../08-crosscutting-concepts/security/node-bff.md)

- NODE-BFF-01: The BFF logs users in, holds their tokens and serves the frontend; it has no business logic.
- NODE-BFF-02: OIDC login uses `openid-client` 6 with authorization code and PKCE.
- NODE-BFF-03: Sessions live server-side behind a `SessionStore` outgoing port, backed by Redis or Postgres, never by process memory.
- NODE-BFF-04: The session cookie is `__Host-session; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`, without `Domain`.
- NODE-BFF-05: The cookie holds only the session id.
- NODE-BFF-06: Every cookie-authenticated unsafe request is CSRF-protected with the cookie and header names the frontends expect: cookie `XSRF-TOKEN`, header `X-XSRF-TOKEN`.
- NODE-BFF-07: Sessions have explicit lifetimes, and the tokens stay server-side.
- NODE-BFF-08: Logout ends the session in the BFF and at the IdP.
- NODE-BFF-09: Every HTML response carries a CSP with a fresh per-response nonce; nothing caches HTML.
- NODE-BFF-10: A Node BFF is adopted only with its threat model and tests.
- NODE-BFF-11: The pre-login state of an anonymous caller is bounded.

## [NestJS: Testing](../08-crosscutting-concepts/testing/nestjs.md)

- NEST-TEST-01: Tests run on Vitest 5 with `unplugin-swc`; never Jest.
- NEST-TEST-02: A test that starts a container is a `*.it.test.ts`; everything else is a `*.test.ts`.
- NEST-TEST-03: Doubles of contracts are `mock<Contract>()` from `vitest-mock-extended` 6, typed by the port or use-case interface.
- NEST-TEST-04: Domain and application tests never start Nest.
- NEST-TEST-05: REST adapter tests run the controller inside Nest and Fastify with the production pipe and filter, and send requests with `app.inject()`.
- NEST-TEST-06: Persistence adapters are tested against a real PostgreSQL with the real migrations (TEST-ARCH-04).
- NEST-TEST-07: Containers are started once per test run and shared.
- NEST-TEST-08: Test data is deterministic (TEST-TDD-16).
- NEST-TEST-09: No fixed waits.
- NEST-TEST-10: The architecture check runs on every build and proves that it can fail (ARCH-ENF-02).
- NEST-TEST-11: The OpenAPI spec test compares the generated document with the committed file (nestjs-openapi.md).
- NEST-TEST-12: Main paths have system tests (TEST-ARCH-05, TEST-TDD-06).
- NEST-TEST-13: Coverage is reported, not gated.
- NEST-TEST-14: Tags select test groups, never skip them.
